questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code decides which devices fall inside a percentage rollout? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
An operator saves the flag file with percent=abc for one flag. What does the running service do on the next reload tick?
choices: It enables that flag for 0% of devices and applies all other rules from the file
It logs a warning and keeps applying the previously loaded rules for every flag
It stops the reload timer because the exception escapes the scheduled task
It skips only the bad flag and applies the new values of the other flags

questions.prompt: A flag has percent=100, models="" and kill=true. What does isEnabled return for any device?
choices: True, because 100 percent includes every device
True for devices whose model is listed, which is none, so all devices
False, because the kill check returns before the percentage is considered
It depends on whether the file has been reloaded since the flag was added

questions.prompt: reloadIfChanged is synchronized, while isEnabled is not. What is the consequence for device ingest threads?
choices: Ingest threads block whenever a reload is in progress
Two reloads can run at once and corrupt the rules map
isEnabled can observe a half-parsed rule set during a reload
Ingest threads read the current immutable map through a volatile field and never wait for a reload
